regions.text: 然性に様つたのである。

quote.translation: And it was because it is the possible of not being that it ran counter to the necessity belonging to the whole of possibilities.

regions.text: さうしてこれらの偶然の三つの意味は決して個々に分離してゐるのではなく、深然として一に融合してゐる。

quote.translation: These three meanings of the contingent are by no means separate from one another; they are fused, undivided, into one.

regions.text: 「個物および個々の事象」の核心的意味は「一の系列と他の系列との避逅といふことに存し、避逅の核心意味は避逅しないことも可能であることすなはち「無いことの可能」といふここに存してゐる。さうしてこれらすべてを原本的に規定してゐる偶然性の根源的意味は、一者としての必然性に對する他者の措定といふことである。

quote.translation: The core meaning of "the individual thing and the individual event" lies in "the Encounter of one series with another series", and the core meaning of Encounter lies in the fact that it is also possible not to encounter (kaikō, 邂逅), that is, in "the possible of not being".

regions.text: 必然性とは同一性すなはち一者の様相にほかならない。

quote.translation: The originary meaning of contingency, which primordially determines all of these, is the positing of an other over against necessity as the one.

regions.text: 偶然性は一者と他者の二元性のあるところに初めて存するのである。

quote.translation: Necessity is nothing other than identity, the modality of the one, and contingency first exists only where there is the duality of the one and the other.

regions.text: アリストラレスが偶然とは「自己としてではなく他のものとして』（oixiairiinx'iErepor）存在する（Aristoteles,Meta-phyicanD.30,10352）と云ひ、ヘーゲルが偶然前なものとは一般にその存在の根據を「自己自身の中にではなくて他者の中に』（nichtinsichselbst,sonderninAnderem）有つてゐる知きものである（Hegel,Encyklopidi

quote.translation: This is precisely why Aristotle says that the contingent exists "not as itself but as another" (οὐχ ᾗ αὐτὸ ἀλλ' ᾗ ἕτερον) (Aristoteles, Metaphysica, Δ 30, 1025a), and why Hegel says that the contingent is in general what has the Ground of its existence "not in itself but in another" (nicht in sich selbst, sondern in Anderem) (Hegel, Encyklopädie, hrsg. v. Bolland, 1906, § 145, Zusatz S. 193).

quote.translation: The origin of the individual thing goes back to the dual positing of the other over against the one; Encounter is nothing other than the Encounter of two independent elements; and the possible of not being presupposes duality, as something based on the choice of the one or the other.
